title: getConnector() masks every string credential field to only the last 4 characters
description: ConnectorService.getConnector() builds maskedCredentials by replacing all but the trailing 4 characters of each string credential with '*'. Values of length <= 4 are fully masked as '****'.
steps: Call ConnectorService.getConnector(integrationId, user) directly with a mocked config containing credentials {accessToken, refreshToken, apiKey: 'abcd'}
Inspect the returned maskedCredentials object
expectedResult: accessToken/refreshToken show '*' repeated for (length-4) characters followed by the real last 4 characters; apiKey ('abcd', length 4) is fully masked to '****'. Raw values never appear in the returned object.

title: startOAuthFlow() generates a 32-byte cryptographically random hex state token
description: ConnectorService.startOAuthFlow uses crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') for the CSRF state parameter, keyed in Redis as oauth-state:<state> with a 10-minute TTL bound to integrationId/organizationId/userId/integrationType.
steps: Call startOAuthFlow() twice for the same connector/user
Compare the two returned state values
Inspect the Redis key written for each call
expectedResult: Each call returns a distinct 64-character hex string; the Redis entry oauth-state:<state> stores integrationId, organizationId, userId and integrationType with a TTL of exactly 600000ms.

title: verifyWebhookSignature() computes the correct HMAC-SHA256 for each connector type's header scheme
description: webhook.routes.ts verifyWebhookSignature() branches per connectorType: GitHub uses x-hub-signature-256 = 'sha256=' + hmac, Slack prefixes the HMAC input with 'v0:<timestamp>:' and rejects timestamps more than 300s old, the generic fallback accepts either raw or 'sha256='-prefixed digest.
steps: Compute HMAC-SHA256 of a sample payload with a known secret for github, slack, and the generic/default branch
Call verifyWebhookSignature() with matching and non-matching signature headers for each branch
For slack, also call it with a timestamp older than 300 seconds
expectedResult: Matching signatures return true for each connector type; a wrong signature returns false; a Slack request with a stale timestamp (>300s) is rejected as a replay attempt regardless of signature validity.

title: ensureValidToken() refreshes the access token only when within the 5-minute expiry buffer
description: OAuthConnector.ensureValidToken() compares creds.expiryDate against Date.now() + a 5-minute buffer before deciding to call refreshToken(). Connectors with no expiryDate (e.g. GitHub) are treated as never expiring.
steps: Call ensureValidToken() with expiryDate 10 minutes in the future
Call it again with expiryDate 2 minutes in the future (inside the 5-minute buffer)
Call it with expiryDate undefined and no refreshToken
expectedResult: Case 1 returns the existing accessToken without calling refreshToken(). Case 2 calls refreshToken(refreshToken) and returns the new token. Case 3 (no expiry) returns the existing token without attempting a refresh.

title: GoogleDriveConnector.listFiles() builds a Drive query scoped to the given folder and excludes trashed files
description: listFiles() always appends 'trashed = false' and "'<folderId>' in parents" to the Drive API q parameter, and clamps pageSize to a maximum of 100.
steps: Call listFiles({ folderId: 'abc123', pageSize: 500 })
Inspect the constructed query string sent to the Drive API
expectedResult: The q parameter includes "'abc123' in parents and trashed = false"; pageSize sent to Google is clamped to 100, not 500.

title: AllIntegrationsContent category filter and count badges only count connectors matching categoryKey
description: countByCategory() and the filtered/activeConnectors/inactiveConnectors derivations in AllIntegrationsContent.jsx must reflect only connectors whose categoryKey matches the selected sidebar item, or the 'all' bucket.
steps: Render AllIntegrationsContent with a mixed catalog (identity_iam, cloud_infrastructure, productivity_collaboration types, some isEnabled=true)
Click the 'Identity & IAM' sidebar category
Read the badge count next to each sidebar item and the number of cards rendered
expectedResult: Only connectors with categoryKey === 'identity_iam' render as cards; the sidebar badge count for that category equals the number of matching connectors; the 'All Integrations' badge always equals the full catalog length.

title: GenericIntegrationCard derives enabled/needsReauth state correctly from catalogData flags
description: initialStatus.enabled requires isConnected && connectionStatus === 'active' && !tokenExpired; needsReauth is true if tokenExpired OR connectionStatus is 'error' or 'pending'.
steps: Render GenericIntegrationCard with catalogData { isConnected: true, connectionStatus: 'active', tokenExpired: true }
Render again with { isConnected: true, connectionStatus: 'error', tokenExpired: false }
expectedResult: Both cases render as NOT enabled (tokenExpired or error state overrides connected+active) and both set needsReauth = true, surfacing a reconnect prompt instead of a healthy 'connected' badge.

title: SophosCentralConnector caches its OAuth2 access token across model groups instead of re-authenticating per API family
description: getToken() caches the token returned by the client-credentials grant and reuses it (tokenCache.expiresAt > now + 60s) across the endpoint, alert, audit, and firewall model groups within a single collect() run, rather than re-authenticating once per group.
preconditions: Sophos Central connector configured with valid tenant client-credentials
steps: Enable both endpoint_status and security_alert models on a single collect() call
Count calls to the id.sophos.com/api/v2/oauth2/token endpoint
expectedResult: Exactly one token request is made for the whole collect() run, reused for both model groups.

title: A 401 from a Sophos evidence API triggers exactly one forced token refresh and retry, never a second retry
description: call() catches an HTTP 401, forces getToken(true) once, and retries the same request with retryAuth=false. If the retried request also 401s, the error propagates without a further retry attempt.
steps: Mock /endpoint/v1/endpoints to return 401 on the first call and 200 on the second
Run collect() with only endpoint_status enabled and count both token fetches and endpoint call attempts
Repeat with the endpoint route always returning 401
expectedResult: First scenario: 2 token fetches (initial + forced refresh), 2 endpoint attempts, model completes successfully. Second scenario: exactly 2 endpoint attempts total (no third retry), model marked permission_denied/NO_PERMISSION.

title: discoverTenant() rejects partner/organization-level credentials and whoami responses missing a tenant id
description: SophosCentralConnector V1 requires idType === 'tenant' from the global whoami endpoint. Partner or organization-scoped credentials, or a tenant response missing an id, must fail with a clear, specific message rather than proceeding with the wrong credential scope.
steps: Mock whoami to return idType: 'partner', then idType: 'organization', then idType: 'tenant' with no id field
Call testConnection() for each case
expectedResult: All three cases return { valid: false } with a message stating tenant credentials are required (identifying the received idType) or that whoami returned no tenant ID.

title: validateApiHost() only accepts an HTTPS *.central.sophos.com origin for the discovered data-region host
description: validateApiHost() rejects a missing dataRegion host, a different domain entirely, and a suffix-spoofed lookalike domain (e.g. sophos.com.attacker.example.com), returning only the URL origin when the host genuinely ends with .central.sophos.com over https.
steps: Mock whoami with apiHosts.dataRegion omitted
Mock whoami with apiHosts.dataRegion set to a suffix-spoofed lookalike domain
Call testConnection() for each case
expectedResult: Both cases return { valid: false } with a message identifying an invalid or missing data-region API host; no request is ever issued to the spoofed host.

title: classifyError()'s RATE_LIMITED branch is currently unreachable for Sophos because apiCall() swallows the HTTP 429 status on final retry exhaustion
description: A persistent 404 correctly classifies as unsupported/API_NOT_AVAILABLE. A persistent 429 is retried by BaseConnector.apiCall() with real exponential backoff (~15s total across 4 attempts) but never assigns lastError in its 429 branch, so the final thrown error is the generic 'API call failed after retries' — which does not match classifyError()'s /HTTP 429/ pattern, and the model is marked TRANSIENT_OR_API_ERROR instead of the intended RATE_LIMITED.
steps: Mock /firewall/v1/firewalls to always return 404 — run collect() with sophos_firewall enabled
Mock /common/v1/alerts to always return 429 — run collect() with security_alert enabled (allow ~15-20s for real backoff sleeps)
expectedResult: 404 case: status 'unsupported', code 'API_NOT_AVAILABLE'. 429 case (current behavior, flagged as a gap): status 'error', code 'TRANSIENT_OR_API_ERROR', message does not contain 'HTTP 429'.

title: numberedPages() aggregates every page up to page.pages.total and falls back to stopping on the first empty page when total is absent
description: The firewall inventory fetch loops pages 1..100, stopping either once pageNumber >= pages.total (when total is numeric) or as soon as a page returns zero items (when total is absent/non-numeric).
steps: Mock a 2-page firewall response with pages.total = 2, one firewall per page
Mock a firewall response with no pages.total field: page 1 returns one item, page 2 returns zero items
expectedResult: First case: both pages fetched exactly once each, both firewalls present in the resulting inventory. Second case: exactly 2 page requests made, stopping at the first empty page.

title: sophos_endpoint_posture skips endpoints missing required fields and reports a partial status with an explicit skip count
description: An endpoint missing health.overall, a boolean tamperProtectionEnabled, or an array assignedProducts is excluded from posture evidence and counted as skipped; the model result status becomes 'partial' (not 'complete') with code INCOMPLETE_ENDPOINT_FIELDS and a message stating how many were skipped.
steps: Mock 4 endpoints: one fully valid, one missing health, one with a non-boolean tamperProtectionEnabled, one with assignedProducts not an array
Run collect() with sophos_endpoint_posture enabled
expectedResult: Exactly 1 posture evidence item is produced (the valid endpoint). modelResults for sophos_endpoint_posture shows status 'partial', authoritative false, itemCount 1, code INCOMPLETE_ENDPOINT_FIELDS, message citing 3 skipped endpoints.

title: firmware-upgrade-check requests are batched in chunks of at most 1000 firewall IDs
description: For tenants with more than 1000 firewalls, the firmware-upgrade-check POST is called once per 1000-ID chunk (offset stepping by 1000), never with more than 1000 IDs in a single request body.
steps: Mock a firewall inventory of 1500 firewalls across a single page
Run collect() with sophos_firewall_posture enabled and capture every firmware-upgrade-check request body
expectedResult: Exactly 2 firmware-upgrade-check calls are made: the first with 1000 firewall IDs, the second with the remaining 500.

title: Sync-status is queried once per distinct firewall group, excludes ungrouped firewalls, and a single failing group is marked partial without discarding groups that succeeded
description: sophos_firewall_sync_posture computes the set of unique group.id values across all firewalls and calls the sync-status endpoint once per group (not once per firewall). Firewalls with no group.id never appear in sync-posture evidence. If one group's call fails, the model result is 'partial'/PARTIAL_GROUP_SYNC_STATUS with the successfully-fetched groups' evidence still emitted.
steps: Mock 4 firewalls: 2 in group-a, 1 in group-b, 1 with no group at all
Run collect() with sophos_firewall_sync_posture enabled and count sync-status calls per group
Repeat with group-b's sync-status call returning 403
expectedResult: First case: exactly one sync-status call for group-a and one for group-b; 3 sync-posture items (for the 3 grouped firewalls), none for the ungrouped one. Second case: modelResults status 'partial', authoritative false, code PARTIAL_GROUP_SYNC_STATUS, itemCount reflecting only the group that succeeded.

title: Disabling every model except sophos_tenant makes zero calls to the endpoint, alert, audit, or firewall APIs
description: collect({ enabledModels: ['sophos_tenant'] }) must only perform the token + whoami discovery calls and synthesize the single sophos_tenant evidence item — no request should ever be issued to the endpoint, common/alerts, audit, or firewall API families.
steps: Register a catch-all mock route that throws if called for anything other than the token/whoami endpoints
Run collect({ enabledModels: ['sophos_tenant'] })
expectedResult: No unexpected route is ever hit; exactly one evidence item (sophos_tenant) is returned; syncMetadata.attemptedCanonicalModels === ['sophos_tenant'].

title: redact() strips both the configured client secret and the cached access token from any surfaced error text
description: Even if an upstream error response happens to echo back the caller's own bearer token or client secret, redact() must remove both values from every warning/error message and log line before they reach syncMetadata or the collection result.
preconditions: A model API mock deliberately echoes the client secret and access token back in its error body
steps: Mock /common/v1/alerts to return a 403 whose error body contains the literal client secret and access token
Run collect() and serialize the full result to JSON
expectedResult: The serialized result contains neither the client secret nor the access token; both are replaced with '[REDACTED]'.
